content:
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates decline; increase downward bias in forecast, especially for short-term (1-7d) horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated drop; cap forecast decline to 1.5x prior peak or use sentiment to dampen overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not just historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility in early days (1-5d) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing or decay factor to early forecast values.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often forecasts too much upside; reduce forecast by 10-20% if sentiment > 0.8 and price > 1.5x recent mean.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast by 10-20% if sentiment < 0.3 and price < 0.5x recent mean.
